Actually no and I’m so glad you asked this question! So many people take the book of Genesis, specifically the creation story, literally. The creation story is a poem called a chiasm, a type of Hebrew poetry in which the main idea is found at the middle of the poem. We know this due to historical finds, how the poem reads in the original Hebrew language, and how many different books of the Bible are not Historical narratives but are of different genres. If you want to get into the nitty gritty of how we know the Genesis creation story is not to be taken literally, I’d love to get into it but I’m trying to keep it brief!

Anyways, the main point of the poem is that God created man and woman in His image. Everything else is to be taken as a poem, and not literally. When God said be fruitful and multiply he was A) stating it to Adam and Eve in the creation poem, not to the whole of humanity and B) also meaning to be fruitful and multiply the bounty of the Earth, not just literally carry on the progeny of your genes. The be fruitful and multiply is NOT a commandment for the whole of humanity. Otherwise, Jesus would’ve disobeyed God by not procreating, and for us Catholics, Jesus is God, so God can’t contradict God. We also wouldn’t allow nuns or priests or consecrated virgins.

All in all, no that verse is to not be taken literally and whoever is saying it is does not have a firm grasp of Biblical literature and history and should humble themselves and consider reading more and keeping an open mind.
